evidence.description: The WS2 relabel execution record (specs/091-anchor-comparison-integrity/records/standings-relabel-execution-2026-11-21.md), sections 1-2.

falsification_tests: A sign in the standings record absent from the log or present twice; a log entry whose reading, class, or flag differs from the standings record's row for that sign.
claims.text: The log carries every one of the 94, exactly once, as the standings record states them: every strict-core reading in the executed standings (the WS2 relabel execution record: 5 E + 65 I + 4 R + 3 P + 17 U) appears exactly once in the inference log, with its sign, its reading as recorded, its executed class, and its source-diversity flag as that record states them. This does not establish: that the standings are correct; the log transcribes the record of record, it does not re-derive it.

evidence.description: Spec section 3.1 (sources of record) and section 3.2 (schema: every item cites a verbatim basis_span).

falsification_tests: A filed basis element with no corresponding log item (the completeness check of TC-099-02 enumerates the checkable families mechanically); or a log item whose basis_span does not occur in the entry's basis_as_filed.
claims.text: The log is complete against the filed bases, and contains nothing they do not state: every evidence element stated in a reading's filed basis (the appendix row as filed from the register, cross-checked against the frozen register snapshot and the falsifiers annex's evidence line) appears in that reading's log entry as an item citing the verbatim basis clause it was extracted from; and no log item cites a clause its entry's filed basis does not contain. This does not establish: that the filed bases are complete derivations; where a basis is truncated or thin, the log records the truncation or thinness, it does not repair it.

evidence.description: Spec section 3.3 (item kinds and typing rules) and section 3.4 (ambiguity rule).

falsification_tests: A (b) item whose cited basis clause, read plainly, states primary evidence and no other reading or construct; an ambiguous item with no reason; a named target absent from the cited clause and from the records the spec names as the item's source.
claims.text: Every item is typed by the filed basis, and ambiguity is recorded, never resolved silently: each item is typed (a) primary evidence, (b) another reading or a candidate-system construct used as evidence, or ambiguous, under the typing rules of spec section 3.3; every (b) item names the readings it depends on, or records that the basis names no target; every (b) and ambiguous item carries a reason tied to the basis text; and every (b) classification was verified by reading the filed basis clause it cites. This does not establish: that a (b) typing makes an item worthless; it makes the item dependent, which is what the audit measures; several (b) items record real co-occurrence whose raw counts the log also carries as (a) items.

evidence.description: Spec section 4 (removal, recomputation, components) and the reference implementation in tools/inference_log.py.

falsification_tests: The determinism recomputation (TC-099-03's implementation, run over the real log at Stage 2) differing from the filed audit table on any reading or component; or the audit tool's input manifest naming a source beyond the log and the class-rule records.
claims.text: The audit is a pure function of the log: the Q3 graph audit's per-reading outcomes and component list reproduce exactly from the log file, the executed standings it carries, and the class rules of spec section 4.2, with no other input; an independent implementation of those rules recomputes the filed audit table without difference. This does not establish: that the class rules are the uniquely right ones; they are the adjudication's, applied as recorded, so the audit measures what the program's own rules imply.

evidence.description: The relabel execution record's class vocabulary and addendum rule (specs/091-anchor-comparison-integrity/records/standings-relabel-execution-2026-11-21.md, sections 1 and 4).

falsification_tests: An outcome inconsistent with the rules applied to the log's items for that reading; a filed outcome missing its sensitivity divergence where the two treatments differ; or a standings record changed citing this audit as its basis.
claims.text: The audit applies the adjudication's class rules and moves nothing: each reading's outcome is stated in the vocabulary of spec section 4.2 (class unchanged / basis weakened with the losses named / class would change with the destination named), computed under the relabel execution record's class definitions and the reclassification form of its addendum; both the primary treatment (ambiguous retained) and the sensitivity treatment (ambiguous removed) are computed and any divergence reported; and no standing, anchor, or register entry is altered by the audit or by any record of this package. This does not establish: that a 'class would change' outcome changes the class; it is a report to a further adjudication, which this package is not.

evidence.description: Spec section 4.3 (components) and the dependency record's closure list (specs/091-anchor-comparison-integrity/records/dependency-record-2026-11-21.md).

falsification_tests: A cycle in the log's named-target (b)-graph absent from the completion record's component list; an open end omitted from the list; or a cyclicity claim in the package not backed by the computed components.
claims.text: Cycles are computed, not asserted: the completion record states the strongly connected components of the log's (b)-graph (named-target edges) as computed, and lists the (b) items whose targets the filed bases do not name as open ends; no record of this package describes the dependency structure among the 94 as acyclic or as cyclic beyond that computation and that list. This does not establish: that an unnamed-target edge conceals no cycle; the record states the limit on its face, which is what replaces the dependency record's 'not established in either direction' with a bounded, checkable statement.

evidence.description: Spec section 5 and the standings supplement section 2 (specs/091-anchor-comparison-integrity/records/standings-supplement-2026-11-21.md).

falsification_tests: A (b) item in M267's log entry missing from the statement; a slot marker named in the statement that M267's entry does not carry; or a retest result, in any form, anywhere in this package's records.
claims.text: The M267 dependency statement is exact to the log, and no retest is run: the statement names every (b)-type premise in M267's log entry, with its kind and its named targets, states which of M267's (a) items survive removal, and states what a dependency-aware retest must hold fixed or exclude; this package runs no M267 retest and designs none in executable detail. This does not establish: that M267's reading is false; it establishes what its filed basis depends on, which is the input a future retest commission needs.

evidence.description: The owner's commission of 2026-11-21 and the program's standing execution discipline (as recorded for Spec 098, D-098-4).

falsification_tests: A run executed on the coordination VM or the mini-server; a stage record claiming a check whose raw output is not filed or hashed in the package's records; or a reported verdict that is a wrapper state rather than the payload's own record.
claims.text: Execution discipline: venue, index, payload verdicts: all execution runs on tower-compute in fresh clones under ~/glossa-work/; every build, check, and audit run of this package is indexed in the spec's records with its raw output or its hash; and every reported verdict is the run's own payload verdict, never a wrapper or transport state. This does not establish: that a complete index proves the runs were correct; it proves they are all on the record, which is what makes their correctness checkable.
